text.content: Contigo GmbH's support agent can already answer questions from the knowledge base you connected in Sprint 2. It can explain loan products, eligibility criteria, and application requirements using retrieved evidence.

text.content: This is the difference between retrieval and tool use. RAG gives the agent access to documented knowledge. Tools give it access to capabilities such as live lookups, calculations, APIs, databases, and deterministic workflows.

What tools are

text.content: A tool is a capability the AI Agent can invoke while processing a request.

rich_text.plain_text: A tool is a capability the AI Agent can invoke while processing a request.

text.content: Three common categories are useful for Contigo:

rich_text.plain_text: Three common categories are useful for Contigo:
Information tools:

text.content: Query live or structured data, for example an application-status service.

rich_text.plain_text: Query live or structured data, for example an application-status service.
Action tools:

text.content: Trigger a controlled operation in another system or workflow.

rich_text.plain_text: Trigger a controlled operation in another system or workflow.
Computational tools:

text.content: Perform deterministic calculations rather than asking the language model to calculate approximately.

rich_text.plain_text: Perform deterministic calculations rather than asking the language model to calculate approximately.

The agent tool loop

text.content: A tool-enabled agent follows a repeated decision loop:

rich_text.plain_text: A tool-enabled agent follows a repeated decision loop:
Reason:

text.content: Determine what information or action is needed.

rich_text.plain_text: Determine what information or action is needed.
Act:

text.content: Select an appropriate tool and provide its required inputs.

rich_text.plain_text: Select an appropriate tool and provide its required inputs.
Observe:
Read the tool result.
Continue or answer:

text.content: Call another tool if necessary, or produce the final response.

Why tool descriptions matter

text.content: The AI Agent chooses tools from their names, descriptions, input schemas, the system message, and the current conversation. If two tools have vague or overlapping descriptions, the model may call the wrong one or call a tool when no tool is needed.

rich_text.plain_text: The AI Agent chooses tools from their names, descriptions, input schemas, the system message, and the current conversation. If two tools have vague or overlapping descriptions, the model may call the wrong one or call a tool when no tool is needed.

rich_text.plain_text: A strong tool description therefore states:

when it should be used;
what input is required;
what it must
not

Takeaway:

text.content: RAG gives the agent documented knowledge. Tools extend the same n8n AI Agent with capabilities that are not contained in static documents. Good architecture starts by giving one agent a small, clearly described toolset before adding more agents or orchestration complexity.
